summary: In this story, a boy who keeps a nightly journal of the stars and constellations he observes from his rooftop ends up helping his school identify a newly visible comet.
introduce: Show the title “The Boy Who Collected Stars” and ask, “What do you think will happen in this story, and why?” Explain that good readers use clues in the text together with what they already know to make inferences.

keyTerms.def: a group of stars that forms a pattern or shape in the night sky
to watch something carefully and closely
to write down information so that it is not forgotten

challengeTerms.def: a scientist who studies stars, planets, and other objects in space
a bright object made of ice and dust that travels through space and sometimes passes near Earth
always done in the same careful way, without changing

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that keeping a careful record of something every day, even when nothing exciting happens, is a waste of time? Use evidence from the story to explain.
Explain how Tariq's habits as a careful observer helped lead to the discovery of the comet.
struggling: Read the first part of the story aloud together, review constellation, observe, and record, and let weak readers answer “What clue tells you that?” questions using sentence starters.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses astronomer, comet, and consistent to make an inference that the story does not state and support it with two clues.
